//: THE PROBLEM IR CONTRACT -- one artefact, read by both languages.
This file is to `docs/contracts/problem-ir.md` what
`app/expressions/catalogue.json` is to the expression core: the prose
says what a model MEANS, this says what a validator may accept. The
server reads it at import time (app/ir/contract.py) and the client
restates it as TypeScript (frontend/src/ir/contract.ts); a vitest
parity test (frontend/src/ir/parity.test.ts) reads THIS file off disk
and deep-compares the two. Change either side alone and that fails.
`rules` is the complete list of reasons an IR can be refused. Each
entry carries `where`: `shape` means the rule is decidable from the
document alone (app/ir/validate.py's check_shape, and the client's
validate.ts), `domain` means it needs the domain's rows and so only
the server can judge it. `backend/tests/ir_fixtures.json` carries at
least one invalid IR per code and a test asserts the two lists are
the same set -- so a rule declared here with no fixture, or a fixture
for a rule not declared here, is a test failure.
`filterOperators` is deliberately a SUBSET of the expression
catalogue's `operators`, not a second table: app/ir/contract.py
asserts every name here exists there, and which of them a given
attribute accepts comes from that catalogue's `operatorsByType`.
There is one operator vocabulary on this platform.
`version` is the version this platform writes; `acceptedVersions` the
ones it reads. Version 2 is version 1 plus what Phase 10 adds, so a
version 1 document is valid as it stands (app/ir/models.py upgrade_v1
only restamps it).
`functions` is the closed catalogue a `fn` term names (version 2):
each a function of one argument, labelled with its curvature over its
whole domain (`convex`, `concave` or `neither`), whether it only rises
or falls, and where it is defined. The labels are what curvature
detection composes; the domain is what the compiler holds an argument's
bounds to. Only a global nonlinear solver (SCIP) takes a model that
applies one to a decision.

rules.text: the IR is a JSON object
`version` is present
`version` is a version this platform expresses
every required top-level key is present
no key beyond the contract's -- at the top level, on a declaration, on a constraint, on a binding, on a filter or on a term
`sets` is an array
each set is an entity type name matching the name pattern
a set is named once
`relationships` is an array
each relationship is a relationship type name matching the name pattern
a relationship is named once
`parameters` is an object keyed by parameter name
each parameter key matches the name pattern
each parameter declaration is an object
a parameter declares `index` as an array of set names
every set a parameter is indexed by is declared in `sets`
`variables` is an object keyed by variable name
a model declares at least one variable
each variable key matches the name pattern
each variable declaration is an object
a variable declares `index` as an array of set names
every set a variable is indexed by is declared in `sets`
a variable declares a `domain`
a variable's `domain` is one this version solves
`lower` and `upper` are numbers with lower <= upper, and belong only to an integer or continuous variable
`constraints` is an array
each constraint is an object
a constraint's `id` matches the name pattern
a constraint id is used once
a constraint that is not a scheduling rule states `left`, `relation` and `right`; a declared but unexpressed constraint is not a model
a constraint's `relation` is one this version expresses
a constraint's `severity` is `hard` or `soft`
a soft constraint carries a positive integer `weight`; a hard one carries none
each index binding is an object
a binding's `index` matches the name pattern
an index name is bound once in a scope
a binding's `set` is declared in `sets`
`forall` and a sum's `over` are arrays binding between one index and the limit
a binding's `via` is an object
a `via`'s `rel` is declared in `relationships`
a `via` names exactly one of `from` or `to`, and it is an index name
a `via`'s anchor index is already bound where the traversal starts
a `via`'s `depth` is one this version walks
a binding's `where` is an array of filters
each filter names an `attr`, an `op` and a `value`
a filter's `op` is one of the contract's filter operators
a term, and every object-valued part of one, is in the shape the contract gives it
a term names one of the contract's kinds
a term names exactly one kind
a `const` is a finite number
a `par` or `var` term names something the IR declares
a `par` or `var` is subscripted with as many indices as it is declared with
every index a term uses is bound by an enclosing `forall` or `over`
an index used at a position is bound to the set declared at that position
a `sum` carries a body term and an `over`
an `add` has at least one summand
a `mul` has exactly two factors
a `mul` in a lexicographic objective has at most one factor that contains a variable
a rule or a weighted objective term is at most quadratic: no product of more than two variables
a term nests no deeper than the limit
an IR holds no more terms than the limit
an IR serialises to no more than the byte limit
`objective`, when present, is an object
an objective's `sense` is `minimize` or `maximize`
an objective's `mode` is `weighted` or `lex`; omit it for a weighted sum
an objective carries a non-empty `terms` array
each objective term carries an `id`, an integer `weight` and an `expression`
an objective term id is used once
every declared set is an entity type of the problem's domain
every declared relationship is a relationship type of the problem's domain
a `via`'s anchor and bound sets are the relationship type's own endpoint types, the right way round
a repeated `via` walks a relationship whose two ends are the same entity type
every declared parameter is a parameter of the problem's domain
a parameter's declared index is the domain's own index types, in order
an `attr` names an attribute the bound set declares
an `attr` used as a number has an arithmetic data type
a filter's operator is one the attribute's data type offers
a filter's value is a value of the attribute's data type
a constraint's `when` appears only in a version 2 document
a `when` is an object naming a `var`, its `index`, and optionally `is` (0 or 1)
the variable a `when` names is declared binary
a `when` is on a hard constraint
a constraint with a `when` is linear
a `pwl` term appears only in a version 2 document
a `pwl` names one variable and at least two `[x, y]` points of numbers
a `pwl`'s points are in strictly increasing `x`
a `fn` term appears only in a version 2 document
a `fn` names a function in the contract's `functions` catalogue
a `fn` carries its argument, a term, in `of`
a function's argument is linear: no part of it multiplies two decisions
the `interval` domain appears only in a version 2 document
an interval names its `start`, `end` and `size` (and optionally `presence`) and carries no bounds; no other variable carries those keys
an interval's `start` and `end` are integer variables, and its `presence` a binary one, each declared with the interval's own index
an interval's `size` is a non-negative whole number or a parameter declared with the interval's own index
a `var` term never names an interval; its `start` and `end` variables are the numbers
a `no_overlap` or `cumulative` rule appears only in a version 2 document
a constraint is either an expression (`left`, `relation`, `right`) or exactly one scheduling rule; `no_overlap` carries an `interval` and an `over`, `cumulative` also a `demand` and a `capacity`
a scheduling rule's `interval` names an interval variable
a scheduling rule is hard: no weight, no `when`
a `cumulative`'s `demand` and `capacity` read no variable
a parameter's `uncertainty` appears only in a version 2 document
an `uncertainty` is `{kind: interval, deviation, gamma?}` -- deviation a non-negative fraction of each value, gamma a non-negative number of cells that may deviate at once -- or `{kind: scenarios}`
a variable's `stage` appears only in a version 2 document
a variable's `stage` is 1 (decided now) or 2 (decided once the uncertain data is known), and an interval has none
a constraint's `chance` appears only in a version 2 document
a `chance` is `{epsilon}`, the share of futures the rule may fail in, strictly between 0 and 1
a `chance` is on a hard, linear expression rule with no `when` -- not a soft, conditional, scheduling, connected or route one
a `connected` rule appears only in a version 2 document
a `connected` names `assign`, `units`, `groups` and `via`, and optionally `empty` (`forbidden` or `allowed`), and is not also an expression or inside a `forall`
a `connected` rule's variable is declared binary
a `connected` rule's variable is indexed by its units' index, then its groups' index
a `connected` rule's `via` is a declared relationship
a `connected` rule is hard and unconditional
a `connected` rule's `via` joins the units' entity type to itself
a `route` rule appears only in a version 2 document
a `route` names `visit`, `vehicles`, `stops` and `depot`, and optionally `demand` and `capacity` (both or neither), and is not also an expression or inside a `forall`
a `route` rule's variable is declared binary
a `route` rule's variable is indexed by its vehicles' index, its stops' index, then a third index over the stops
a `route` rule is hard and unconditional
a `route` rule's `travel` is a parameter declared over its stops' set twice, [stop, stop]
a `via` names the edge it walks with `as` in a version 2 document only
a `via`'s `as` is a name not already bound, and not the binding's own index
an edge named by `as` is read with `attr` only, never used as an index or an anchor
an `attr` of an edge walked more than once says how the path combines it in `along`; any other `attr` has no `along`
a parameter's `entity` names a declared set, in a version 2 document, and such a parameter has no uncertainty
a parameter whose values are entities is used as an index or in a filter, never read as a number
an index position is an index name, or `{par, index}` naming a parameter whose values are entities of that position's set
a filter compares with a parameter only as `id` `=` or `!=` a parameter whose values are entities of the binding's set, read at indices already bound
a parameter's `entity` is the value type its parameter definition declares, and a number parameter declares none
